title: fidelity.json
description: Results of the pre-assembly gates (run before Stage 4) and the final Stage 5 verification. Both phases are recorded so the curation loop is auditable. Mirror the same facts into the persona's fidelity-ledger/provenance.md in prose/table form.

projection.description: Held-out projection test. The gate phase runs on top-ranked projectible regularities before assembly; the final phase re-checks the assembled core.

passed.description: False here means re-curate. Assembly is always downstream of passing; a failed gate sends you back to Stage 3, never forward to the template.

recurations.description: How many re-curation loops the gate forced.

by_domain.description: Per-domain projection scores. Low scorers become explicit 'trust this less' caveats in the coverage report.

seed.description: Seed passed to holdout_split.py. Records the split so the test is repeatable.

n_masked.description: Number of masked passages. Must match n_masked in the split holdout_split.py produced.

cost.description: Cost/presence assertion. The hard minimum: if the corpus contains any high-signal cost-bearing refusal or interactional move, the core must contain at least one. Failing this blocks delivery.

total_divergences.description: Every attested incentive-vs-characteristic divergence inventoried at Stage 2.

slated_for_core.description: Confirmed by the cost gate before assembly.

in_core_final.description: Actually present in the assembled core.

logged_out.description: Dropped deliberately, with the reason logged.

missing_unlogged.description: Dropped without a logged reason. Must be 0 at delivery — any non-zero value means go re-curate.

presence_assertion.description: 'fail' blocks delivery. This is the most common way a core ends up articulate but generic.

style.description: Style-match test. Sample passages generated under the core's expression rules PLUS references/voice.md — that pair is the sustained-prose configuration, so that is what gets tested — re-measured with style_metrics.py and compared against held-out originals. At least one sample must be long enough to drift (400+ words); a voice that is right for three sentences and generic by the twelfth is the failure this test exists to catch.

sentence_len_delta.description: Normalised absolute difference from the held-out originals.

avoid_list_violations.description: How many items from voice.md's 'What I never write' section appeared in the generated samples. A cheap binary-ish check that catches drift the distributions blur; anything above 0 means revise voice.md's rules or the generation configuration. Record 0 when the corpus supported no avoid-list.

modulation_reproduced.description: Whether register shifts under pressure/audience/stakes are reproduced, not just the averages. False is a real failure even when the averages match — the modulation is the individuating part.

discrimination.description: Blind register-separation gate. Present only when the persona claims internal variation — per-work, per-period, or per-venue registers. Omit for a single-register persona, where it does not apply. Produced by scripts/discrimination_test.py.

score.description: Fraction of sampled passages correctly assigned to their register, classified blind. >=0.90 the registers are separable and per-register rules are load-bearing; 0.70-0.90 usable, but name the confusable pairs in the coverage report; <0.70 the registers are not distinct in this corpus — collapse them into one honest voice rather than shipping a distinction the persona cannot perform.

seed.description: Sampling seed, so the split is reproducible.

mask_names.description: Whether capitalised mid-sentence tokens were masked. A score obtained with names visible may rest on recognising a cast rather than a register, and only the register survives into use.

confusable_pairs.description: Register pairs confused more than once, e.g. 'c03->c01'. A pair confused repeatedly is one register, not two, whatever the labels say.

style.notes: clipping-under-contest present; 600-word sample held voice to the end (core + voice.md)
